title: German marzipan potatoes
subtitle: Marzipankartoffeln: small marzipan balls rolled in cocoa
excerpt: Marzipankartoffeln are a traditional German Christmas confection, especially associated with the marzipan-making city of Lübeck. Ready-made marzipan is rolled into small ovals, then tumbled through cocoa powder until they look convincingly like tiny new potatoes. They are one of the simplest confections to make and keep well in an airtight tin for two weeks.
sourceNotes: Marzipankartoffeln are a classic German Christmas tradition, particularly associated with the town of Lübeck in Schleswig-Holstein, which has been producing marzipan since at least the 15th century. Niederegger, the best-known Lübeck marzipan maker, has sold marzipan potatoes since the early 20th century. The recipe is widely documented in German home-baking books and food encyclopaedias.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in a single layer then transfer to a container. Defrost at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keep in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.

content.text: German marzipan potatoes are made from ready-made marzipan rolled into small ovals and tumbled in cocoa powder. They require no cooking, set in the fridge, and need nothing more than good-quality marzipan (at least 25% almond content) and cocoa. Adding a small amount of ground cinnamon to the cocoa gives a warmer, spiced flavour that suits the Christmas season.

Knead the {{marzipan}} briefly on a work surface dusted lightly with {{icing-sugar}} until smooth and pliable. Room-temperature marzipan is much easier to handle than cold marzipan from the fridge; leave it out for 30 minutes if it has been refrigerated.

Pinch off pieces of marzipan roughly the size of a large marble, about 12 to 15 g each. Dust your palms lightly with icing sugar and roll each piece into a ball, then pinch one end very slightly and flatten the other to make an irregular oval, the shape of a small new potato. The surface should be slightly rough and uneven, not perfectly smooth. This gives the finished potatoes a more convincing appearance once coated.

Sift {{cocoa-powder}} (and {{cinnamon-ground}} if using) into a bowl. Drop 5 or 6 marzipan shapes at a time into the cocoa and toss to coat thoroughly. Press the cocoa gently into any creases with a fingertip. Tap off the excess and transfer to a baking-paper-lined tray. Continue until all pieces are coated.

Refrigerate for 30 minutes until the cocoa crust has set and the marzipan is firm. Once chilled, transfer to an airtight tin, layering with baking paper to prevent sticking. Serve at room temperature: straight from the fridge the flavour of the marzipan is muted.
